newsitem.title: USA: Dominick's buying two Chicago-area stores.
newsitem.headline: Dominick's buying two Chicago-area stores.

text.p: Dominick's Supermarkets Inc said Tuesday it is acquiring two Chicago-area stores of the Byerly's grocery chain.

"Our purchase of the two Byerly's stores further accelerates our new store opening program, which currently has six new Dominick's Fresh Stores in various stages of construction," Robert Mariano, president, said in a statement. "We'll re-open the Byerly's stores as Dominick's Fresh Stores and complete the conversion of three Dominick's stores to Fresh Stores this quarter."

Earlier, Lund Food Holdings Inc, parent of Lund Food Stores, said it agreed to buy the Byerly's grocery chain for undisclosed terms. Lund had said that the two Chicago-area Byerly's stores were sold to Dominick's.
Dominick's is the second largest supermarket operator in the Chicago area with fiscal 1996 revenues of $2.5 billion and 102 stores operated under the Dominick's and Omni names.
